result:
Post revisions are in and `bun run typecheck` passes. I didn't run the tests or boot the app, so none of the new behaviour has been exercised.

- **Storage:** a `post_revisions` table (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at`) in `db/schema.ts`, with a generated migration `db/migrations/20261019042546_post_revisions`. I didn't run `db:migrate` here. There is also a new `PostRevision` model in `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`.
- **Keeping versions:** `PostController.update` saves the post's previous title, excerpt and body as a revision just before applying the edit. It does this only after authorization and validation pass, so refused edits keep nothing. Creating a post keeps nothing. It also keeps a revision when a save changes nothing, since you said that case isn't checked.
- **History page:** `GET /posts/:id/revisions` is handled by `revisions()` and renders a new `posts/Revisions.tsx` page. Its props are `revisions: [{ id, title, createdAt }]`, newest first. Each revision has a Restore button. The post page has a "History" link, shown only to the author.
- **Restore:** `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` is handled by `restore()`. It saves the post's current version as a new revision, puts the chosen revision's title, excerpt and body back on the post, and redirects to `/posts/:id`. A revision belonging to a different post answers 404.
- **Access:** both new routes sit in the existing `auth` group, so guests go to `/login`. They reuse the `update` policy, so any other signed-in user gets 403.
- **Delete:** `destroy` removes the post's revisions before deleting the post, because of the foreign key. Other posts' revisions are untouched.

I also added a `PostRevisionParamSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` and registered the two routes in `routes/web.ts`.
